classification.classification_note: The observed fault is a sanitizer-visible uninitialized read: `word8_sub3()` logically writes subtraction results into stack buffer `z[8]`, but on x86_64 those writes happen in inline asm that MemorySanitizer does not model, so later C++ reads of `z` stay poisoned unless the buffer is initialized in source.

bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced MemorySanitizer's `use-of-uninitialized-value` against the exact staged Botan checkout `2674d453be668537fcf5cc1ea634659b1aefda9b`. The exact witness is the 114-byte file `20ff20ffff2020ffffffffff2020202020202020202020202020202020202020ffff20ff20ffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff20ffff20ffffff20ffffffffffffffffff20ff2020ff20202020ffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff20ffffffffffffffffff20`. `fuzz()` splits it into two 57-byte big-endian integers, forces the second half odd with `mod.set_bit(0)`, and the guard `mod < 3 || x >= mod` does not reject the pair. In `ct_inverse_mod_odd_modulus()`, that odd 57-byte modulus still has a nonzero top byte, so `mod.sig_words() == 8` and `bigint_cnd_sub()` takes its 8-word block path. Vulnerable `bigint_cnd_sub()` allocates `word z[8];` without initialization, then `word8_sub3()` writes the subtraction result into `z` via x86_64 inline asm that MemorySanitizer cannot see. The subsequent `CT::select(mask, z[j], x[i+j])` at `mp_core.cpp:83` stores a value derived from poisoned `z[j]` into the caller's limb buffer, and `bigint_cnd_abs()` immediately reads that poisoned limb through `word_add()` at `mp_asmi.h:119`, which is the saved crash. The fix initializes the temporary arrays in `bigint_cnd_{sub,add}` so those later reads are defined even when the arithmetic result came from inline asm.

source.code:
const Botan::BigInt x = Botan::BigInt::decode(in, len / 2);
Botan::BigInt mod = Botan::BigInt::decode(in + len / 2, len / 2);
source.description: First project-code materialization of attacker-controlled state on the crashing path: the witness buffer is split into two BigInt operands `x` and `mod` that later drive the odd-modulus inversion routine.
source.value_from: The exact staged `poc` is the 114-byte hex string `20ff20ffff2020ffffffffff2020202020202020202020202020202020202020ffff20ff20ffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff20ffff20ffffff20ffffffffffffffffff20ff2020ff20202020ffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff20ffffffffffffffffff20`. `fuzz()` splits it into two 57-byte big-endian halves: `x = 20ff20ffff2020ffffffffff2020202020202020202020202020202020202020ffff20ff20ffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff` and `mod_raw = ffffff20ffff20ffffff20ffffffffffffffffff20ff2020ff20202020ffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff20ffffffffffffffffff20`.
source.note: Source. These decodes create the attacker-controlled numeric operands; later steps only normalize `mod` and check that the pair is admissible for `ct_inverse_mod_odd_modulus()`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: MemorySanitizer origin. The temporary block-result buffer `z[8]` is allocated on the stack without initialization, and the x86_64 block subtraction helper writes into it in a way MSan does not recognize.
tainted_value_origin.note: The saved trace attributes the origin to allocation of `z` in the stack frame of `bigint_cnd_sub` at `mp_core.cpp:70`; the concrete declaration that creates the uninitialized bytes is line 74.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `bigint_cnd_sub()` uses stack buffer `z[8]` as the destination for the 8-word subtraction helper but does not initialize it in source, so later C++ reads stay poisoned under MSan when the result came from inline asm.
root_cause.note: The staged fix changes this declaration to `word z[8] = { 0 };`, and then routes the scalar remainder path through `z[0]`, making the temporary buffer sanitizer-visible and initialized before any later read.

sink.description: MemorySanitizer crash site. `word_add()` consumes the poisoned limb value propagated out of `bigint_cnd_sub()` and reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` in the x86_64 asm-backed addition helper.
sink.note: The saved run log reports `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at `/src/botan/build/include/botan/internal/mp_asmi.h:119:4` in `Botan::word_add`, called from `bigint_cnd_abs` line 102 and `ct_inverse_mod_odd_modulus` line 240.

parser_admitted.description: The exact 114-byte witness also passes the earlier even-length/size gate at line 57. After `mod.set_bit(0)`, this guard is false because the 57-byte `x` half is smaller than the 57-byte odd `mod` half and `mod >= 3`, so execution reaches `ct_inverse_mod_odd_modulus(x, mod)`.

evidence_limitations: The exact staged vulnerable source that Stage 02 inspected is checkout `2674d453be668537fcf5cc1ea634659b1aefda9b`, not metadata commit `45eea5c4f3d5a582940cb488d660f3cb8ce189dc`.

Runtime disambiguation is disabled in `run_flags.json`, so Stage 02 did not instrument the loop to identify the exact `bits--` iteration or the runtime values of `odd_a` and `underflow`. The trace therefore avoids depending on those unobserved booleans and instead follows the source facts the saved MSan origin already proves.
Stage 02 did not run a fixed build. `patch_resolves` below remains false even though `patch.diff` clearly initializes the temporary arrays in `bigint_cnd_{sub,add}`.

fine_trace.code:
const Botan::BigInt x = Botan::BigInt::decode(in, len / 2);
Botan::BigInt mod = Botan::BigInt::decode(in + len / 2, len / 2);
fine_trace.note: Source. The exact 114-byte witness is split into two 57-byte big-endian integers: `x = 20ff20ffff2020ffffffffff2020202020202020202020202020202020202020ffff20ff20ffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff` and `mod_raw = ffffff20ffff20ffffff20ffffffffffffffffff20ff2020ff20202020ffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff20ffffffffffffffffff20`.
The low bit of the second decoded integer is forced to 1, so the modulus presented downstream is odd even though the raw witness ended with byte `0x20`.
For the exact witness, the modified modulus is still a nonzero 57-byte value at least 3 and `x < mod`, so this guard does not return and execution enters `ct_inverse_mod_odd_modulus(x, mod)`.

The post-`set_bit` modulus still has a nonzero top byte and bit length 456, so `mod.sig_words()` is 8. That size is forwarded into `bigint_cnd_sub()`, making its `blocks = size - (size % 8)` equal 8 and selecting the 8-word block path.

Tainted-value origin and root cause. `bigint_cnd_sub()` allocates temporary limb buffer `z[8]` without initialization, and because `size == 8` the subsequent block loop will use this buffer rather than the scalar remainder path.

fine_trace.var: z, x + i, y + i, carry
fine_trace.code: carry = word8_sub3(z, x + i, y + i, carry);
fine_trace.note: With `size == 8`, the block loop runs once and writes the 8-word subtraction result into `z`. On x86_64 this helper is implemented with inline `sbbq` asm in `mp_asmi.h`, and the patch message plus the saved MSan report show those writes are not visible to MemorySanitizer.

This is the saved MSan origin store. `CT::select` expands to `(from0 & mask) | (from1 & ~mask)`, so it consumes `z[j]` and stores a value derived from that poisoned temporary back into the caller's limb buffer.

Immediately after the subtraction helper returns, `ct_inverse_mod_odd_modulus()` calls `bigint_cnd_abs(underflow, a_w.data(), mod_words)`. This line reads the poisoned limb from step 7 through `word_add` before the following `CT::select` at line 103 could discard it.
Sink. MemorySanitizer reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` at this `word_add` implementation while `bigint_cnd_abs()` consumes the poisoned limb propagated from step 8.

runtime_crash_location.function: Botan::word_add(unsigned long, unsigned long, unsigned long*)

allocation_context.note: The saved MSan trace says the uninitialized value was created by allocation of `z` in the stack frame of `bigint_cnd_sub` at line 70; the concrete array declaration is line 74.

poc.trigger: Running `/bin/arvo run` in the vulnerable ARVO workspace executes `/out/invert /tmp/poc` and reproduces `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` in `Botan::word_add`, with saved stack `word_add -> bigint_cnd_abs -> ct_inverse_mod_odd_modulus -> fuzz`.

format.name: libFuzzer botan invert witness
format.contract: Exact 114-byte binary witness `20ff20ffff2020ffffffffff2020202020202020202020202020202020202020ffff20ff20ffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff20ffff20ffffff20ffffffffffffffffff20ff2020ff20202020ffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff20ffffffffffffffffff20`. `fuzz()` requires an even length no greater than 1024 bytes; this witness is split into two 57-byte big-endian integers, then line 63 forces the second half odd. For this exact input the resulting modulus remains a 57-byte value with `mod.sig_words() == 8` and `x < mod`, so `ct_inverse_mod_odd_modulus(x, mod)` reaches the 8-word `bigint_cnd_sub()` block path that allocates `z[8]` and triggers the saved MSan report.
